title: Seerah
description: General User → Mid. Familiar events, broader basics and short everyday lessons from the life of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Includes migration, community life, leadership, teaching, justice and compassion. All questions are Mid level; no obscure dates or reference-number memorization are required.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires more understanding and simple connections than Beginner, without specialist study. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith reports checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate lessons from the reports, rather than reproduce historical events. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which ordinary work did the Prophet recall doing for people in Makkah?

options.text: Shepherding sheep
Building royal palaces
Collecting taxes for an empire
Commanding a merchant fleet

questions.explanation: The Prophet mentioned tending the sheep of people in Makkah for payment.

questions.question: Which journey is described in the opening of Surah Al-Isra?

options.text: The migration from Makkah to Madinah
From the Sacred Mosque to Al-Aqsa Mosque by night
The journey from Madinah for the Farewell Hajj
The return from Hudaybiyyah to Madinah

questions.explanation: The verse describes the Night Journey between the Sacred Mosque and Al-Aqsa Mosque.

questions.question: Which daily obligation is connected with the account of the Miraj?

options.text: A daily pilgrimage to Makkah
A requirement to fast every day of the year
The five daily prayers
An obligation to remain awake every night

questions.explanation: The narration of the ascent includes the prescription of five daily prayers.

questions.question: What injustice does the Quran recall about believers driven from their homes?

options.text: They refused every form of honest work
They were required to leave because travel was forbidden
They had rejected all belief in Allah
They were expelled for declaring Allah their Lord

questions.explanation: The verse recalls people unjustly driven out for affirming their faith in Allah.

questions.question: What did the Prophet do on learning of An-Najashi's death?

options.text: He led the companions in funeral prayer for him
He declared that the news should be mocked
He treated the death as a reason to abandon prayer
He ordered that no one mention him

questions.explanation: The Prophet announced An-Najashi's death and led a funeral prayer for him.

questions.question: Which mosque did the Prophet establish while staying with Banu Amr ibn Awf on arrival near Madinah?

options.text: Al-Aqsa Mosque
The mosque of Quba
The Sacred Mosque in Makkah
The mosque of Kufa

questions.explanation: The migration account describes the Prophet establishing and praying in the mosque of Quba before continuing into Madinah.

questions.question: Which two groups were brought together through bonds of brotherhood in Madinah?

options.text: The Romans and Persians
The people of Makkah and Pharaoh's court
The Muhajirun and Ansar
The rulers of Yemen and Byzantium

questions.explanation: The Prophet established brotherhood between emigrants and their supporters in Madinah.

questions.question: At Uhud, what did the Prophet instruct the archers about their position?

options.text: Leave as soon as victory appeared likely
Change their position whenever they preferred
Follow anyone collecting belongings from the field
Remain there until he sent for them

questions.explanation: The archers were clearly instructed not to leave their assigned place without the Prophet's direction.

questions.question: What did the Prophet personally do during the work at Al-Khandaq?

options.text: Help carry earth
Stay away from every practical task
Demand that only newcomers work
Treat the digging as entertainment

questions.explanation: The report describes the Prophet carrying earth during the work at the trench.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the Prophet's journey that led to Hudaybiyyah?

options.text: To move permanently to Yemen
To visit the Sacred House for Umrah
To lead the Farewell Hajj
To establish a royal court outside Makkah

questions.explanation: The Muslims approached for pilgrimage rites; negotiations led to the agreement at Hudaybiyyah.

questions.question: Which wife advised the Prophet to begin the concluding rites himself when the companions hesitated at Hudaybiyyah?

options.text: Aishah
Hafsah
Umm Salamah
Sawdah

questions.explanation: Umm Salamah offered practical advice, and the companions followed when the Prophet acted.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet have a seal ring made for correspondence?

options.text: He wished to stop sending any messages
He believed every letter needed a costly gift
He intended the ring to replace the message itself
He was told rulers would not read unsealed letters

questions.explanation: The report connects the seal ring with the accepted way rulers received letters.

questions.question: Which companion was sent to Yemen with instructions about teaching faith, prayer and zakah?

options.text: Muadh ibn Jabal
Bilal ibn Rabah
Anas ibn Malik
Zayd ibn Thabit

questions.explanation: The Prophet gave Muadh a clear sequence for teaching foundational duties in Yemen.

questions.question: Which wife described the Prophet's speech as clear enough for his words to be counted?

options.text: Umm Salamah
Aishah
Hafsah
Zaynab bint Jahsh

questions.explanation: Aishah's description highlights the clarity of the Prophet's communication.

questions.question: When a Bedouin urinated in the mosque, what response did the Prophet direct?

options.text: Leave the place unclean permanently
Encourage the crowd to humiliate him
Restrain the crowd and clean the place with water
Declare the mosque unusable forever

questions.explanation: The Prophet prevented a harsh reaction and directed that the affected place be cleaned.

questions.question: What did the Prophet do when a young Jewish boy who served him became ill?

options.text: He mocked his illness
He refused to acknowledge his condition
He ordered others to frighten him
He visited him

questions.explanation: The narration records the Prophet visiting the boy during his illness.

questions.question: What did the Prophet do when a Jewish funeral procession passed?

options.text: He stood up
He mocked the mourners
He ordered the procession to be insulted
He denied the deceased was a human being

questions.explanation: When told whose funeral it was, he drew attention to the deceased being a human soul.

questions.question: What did the Prophet reject in the case of a socially prominent woman accused of theft?

options.text: The idea that evidence should matter
Special treatment based on social rank
The rights of people without social influence
The principle that wrongdoing should be addressed

questions.explanation: The report warns against excusing the powerful while applying standards only to the weak.

questions.question: What did the Prophet clarify when an eclipse coincided with his son Ibrahim's death?

options.text: The eclipse proved his son controlled the sun
Every eclipse announces the death of a prophet
Eclipses do not occur because of someone's death or birth
People should use the eclipse to predict private events

questions.explanation: The Prophet corrected the claim connecting the eclipse to his son's death.

questions.question: Whom did the Prophet direct to lead the people in prayer during his severe illness?

options.text: Umar ibn al-Khattab
Ali ibn Abi Talib
Bilal ibn Rabah
Abu Bakr

questions.explanation: The narration records the Prophet repeatedly instructing that Abu Bakr lead the prayer.

questions.question: Why was Khadijah's reassurance after the first revelation more than empty praise?

options.text: She recalled the Prophet's established care for relatives and people in need
She promised that difficult experiences could never happen
She dismissed his distress without listening
She based her support only on social status

questions.explanation: Khadijah pointed to known qualities and acts of service while reassuring him.

questions.question: What does the migration account show about reliance on Allah and preparation?

options.text: Trust required abandoning every travel arrangement
Careful arrangements accompanied trust in Allah
Only wealth made the journey possible
Planning meant rejecting divine help

questions.explanation: The account includes practical arrangements for the journey alongside faith and reliance.

questions.question: What reassurance did the Prophet give his companion in the cave?

options.text: Their pursuers had become their protectors
No human danger could ever exist
Allah was with them in support
They should abandon the journey because fear was possible

questions.explanation: The verse recounts the Prophet reassuring his companion of Allah's support.

questions.question: What community purpose is illustrated by brotherhood between the Muhajirun and Ansar?

options.text: Keeping new arrivals permanently excluded
Replacing faith with family rivalry
Making wealth the only basis for belonging
Turning welcome into practical support for newcomers

questions.explanation: The bonds helped connect emigrants with a supportive community in Madinah.

questions.question: What leadership quality is illustrated by the Prophet carrying earth at the trench?

options.text: Sharing the community's effort
Avoiding difficult tasks because of status
Measuring leadership only by comfort
Leaving hardship entirely to others

questions.explanation: His participation provides an example of practical involvement in shared responsibilities.

questions.question: What general lesson can be drawn from the archers' assignment at Uhud?

options.text: Early success makes every instruction irrelevant
A clear responsibility should not be abandoned merely because success seems near
A shared plan works best when no one keeps a role
Personal excitement always overrides an agreed task

questions.explanation: The incident illustrates the importance of maintaining an assigned responsibility.

questions.question: What does accepting a difficult agreement at Hudaybiyyah illustrate?

options.text: The idea that agreements never matter
The belief that every disagreement must become a fight
Patient commitment to a considered peaceful course
The refusal to consider any negotiated solution

questions.explanation: The account shows restraint and commitment amid terms that were difficult for the companions.

questions.question: What does the Quran's instruction to the Prophet to consult companions show?

options.text: A leader must reject every useful suggestion
Seeking advice always proves inability
Only the least experienced person may make decisions
Consultation belongs alongside responsible leadership and trust in Allah

questions.explanation: The verse joins consultation, decision-making and reliance on Allah.

questions.question: What lesson can be drawn from using a seal for letters to rulers?

options.text: Use appropriate practical means to communicate the message
A message never needs to consider how it will be received
Presentation should replace meaningful content
Ordinary communication tools always conflict with faith

questions.explanation: The Prophet used an accepted means for correspondence to reach its intended audience.

questions.question: What teaching approach appears in the instructions to Muadh for Yemen?

options.text: Begin with obscure disagreements before basic belief
Start with foundational belief, then explain central duties
Teach every detail at once regardless of understanding
Avoid explaining prayer and charity

questions.explanation: Muadh was given a sequence beginning with the testimony of faith, then prayer and zakah.

questions.question: What balance appears in the Prophet's response to the Bedouin in the mosque?

options.text: Show kindness by leaving the problem unaddressed
Protect cleanliness by allowing uncontrolled humiliation
Correct the practical problem without needless harshness
Make anger the only teaching method

questions.explanation: The place was cleaned while the crowd's harsh reaction was restrained.

questions.question: What does visiting the sick Jewish boy demonstrate about the Prophet's concern?

options.text: Concern was reserved only for people of high rank
Illness was treated as an opportunity for mockery
Different beliefs made every kind act impossible
Compassion reached someone outside the Muslim community

questions.explanation: The visit demonstrates care toward the boy during his illness.

questions.question: What principle is reflected in the Prophet's response to the Jewish funeral procession?

options.text: Recognition of a person's humanity across religious differences
The idea that grief deserves ridicule
The claim that only wealth gives people dignity
The need to insult every unfamiliar community

questions.explanation: His response drew attention to the deceased being a human soul.

questions.question: Why is excusing the powerful while punishing only the weak a failure of justice?

options.text: Power automatically makes every action right
Social rank must not decide whether a fair standard applies
Rules matter only for those without connections
Respect for leaders requires denying every fault

questions.explanation: The Prophet warned against a double standard favoring socially prominent people.

questions.question: What is important about the Prophet correcting the eclipse claim after Ibrahim's death?

options.text: He accepted every flattering explanation
He treated coincidence as enough proof of a cause
He corrected a false claim even though it appeared to honor his family
He encouraged people to invent signs about him

questions.explanation: The report shows truth taking priority over an unsupported interpretation that could have enhanced personal prestige.

questions.question: What does Anas's account reveal about the Prophet's daily character?

options.text: Kindness only during public speeches
A habit of humiliating helpers
Respect only for wealthy adults
Consideration and restraint in a long working relationship

questions.explanation: Anas remembered years of service without harsh reproach from the Prophet.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet shorten a prayer on hearing a child cry?

options.text: To avoid distressing the child's mother
Because prayer had no importance to him
Because children were forbidden from ever being nearby
To punish the congregation

questions.explanation: He adjusted the length out of concern for the mother while continuing to lead prayer.

questions.question: What distinction appears in Aishah's description of the Prophet's response to wrongs?

options.text: He ignored every moral responsibility
He did not seek revenge for personal injury
He treated all personal irritation as a reason to retaliate
He made personal pride the measure of justice

questions.explanation: Aishah distinguished his restraint over personal offenses from concern for Allah's limits.

questions.question: How did the Prophet respond to food he did not like?

options.text: He humiliated whoever prepared it
He treated every disliked dish as forbidden
He left it without criticizing it
He demanded that everyone dislike the same food

questions.explanation: The report distinguishes personal preference from insulting food or its preparation.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet sometimes repeat his words?

options.text: To prevent anyone from asking questions
To make the message impossible to remember
To replace clear meaning with volume
So listeners could understand properly

questions.explanation: Anas described repetition as a way to make the Prophet's words understood.

questions.question: You need a useful message to reach an unfamiliar audience. Which approach follows the lesson of the Prophet's sealed letters?

options.text: Use an appropriate accepted format without losing the message
Refuse every practical format the audience can receive
Focus on impressive packaging while removing the content
Assume good intentions make delivery irrelevant

questions.explanation: The seal episode supports taking practical steps so communication reaches its audience.

questions.question: A group is arranging an important journey. Which approach reflects the migration account?

options.text: Avoid preparation to prove faith
Prepare routes and responsibilities while trusting Allah
Assume preparation gives complete control of the outcome
Leave everyone unsure about their tasks

questions.explanation: Practical planning can work together with reliance on Allah, as the migration account illustrates.

questions.question: New families join your community with few local contacts. Which action draws on the Madinan brotherhood example?

options.text: Limit welcome to a public photograph
Treat needing help as a permanent disgrace
Connect them with people who can offer real support
Keep them outside every useful network

questions.explanation: The brotherhood example encourages meaningful relationships and practical support.

questions.question: You lead volunteers doing difficult shared work. Which action reflects the trench account?

options.text: Treat your title as a reason to avoid all work
Reserve every hard task for new members
Only criticize others from a comfortable distance
Join the useful effort where you can

questions.explanation: The Prophet's participation at the trench illustrates leadership that shares responsibility.

questions.question: You have a clear, lawful safety role during an event and the team still relies on you. What lesson from Uhud applies?

options.text: Do not abandon the role just because things seem to be going well
Leave without notice when you see something more exciting
Assume early success cancels the agreed plan
Make your role depend entirely on others praising you

questions.explanation: This is a general lesson about dependable responsibility, not a claim that every instruction in every setting must be followed blindly.

questions.question: A considered, lawful agreement is unpopular with your group. Which lesson from Hudaybiyyah is relevant?

options.text: Assume every difficult agreement must be broken
Do not confuse immediate disappointment with a reason to abandon every peaceful commitment
Treat patience as proof of having no principles
Turn disagreement into personal threats

questions.explanation: The episode illustrates patience and commitment through a difficult negotiated situation; it does not make every proposed agreement wise.

questions.question: A leader is deciding an important matter and dismisses all useful advice as weakness. Which Prophetic guidance challenges that attitude?

options.text: Avoid listening so that authority looks stronger
Replace every decision with endless discussion
Consult people, then decide responsibly and rely on Allah
Judge advice only by the speaker's wealth

questions.explanation: The Quran's instruction to the Prophet combines consultation with action and reliance.

questions.question: A newcomer makes a serious but correctable mistake in a shared space. Which approach reflects the mosque incident?

options.text: Ignore the practical problem completely
Invite everyone to insult the newcomer
Make punishment more important than correcting the situation
Address the problem calmly without encouraging humiliation

questions.explanation: The Prophet's response combined a practical remedy with restraint toward the person.

questions.question: A neighbor of another faith is ill and welcomes contact. Which example can guide a considerate visit?

options.text: The Prophet's visit to the sick Jewish boy
The archers' assignment at Uhud
The use of a seal on official letters
The prescription of five prayers during the Miraj

questions.explanation: The visit provides a concrete Seerah example of concern across religious differences.

questions.question: A team wants to excuse a powerful member while blaming weaker members for the same breach. What lesson applies?

options.text: Treat influence as proof of innocence
Use a fair standard rather than favoring connections
Apply accountability only to people without status
Hide the breach because the member is popular

questions.explanation: The Prophet's warning against unequal standards gives a clear lesson about fairness; this scenario concerns ordinary team accountability.

questions.question: A coincidence is being used to make a flattering but unsupported claim about you. Which response follows the eclipse example?

options.text: Encourage it because admiration is useful
Invent extra details to strengthen it
Correct the claim even if it brings you praise
Treat attention as proof that it is true

questions.explanation: The Prophet did not allow an unsupported eclipse explanation to stand for the sake of personal honor.

questions.question: You arrange a community activity involving parents with young children. Which lesson fits the shortened-prayer account?

options.text: Assume a longer activity is always more virtuous
Treat every child's distress as a reason for public blame
Ignore participants' circumstances to preserve your preferred schedule
Consider real burdens when planning the activity

questions.explanation: The account shows concern for another person's difficulty while fulfilling a shared religious activity.

questions.question: Someone offers lawful food that does not suit your taste. Which response follows the Prophet's food manners?

options.text: Decline without insulting the food or the person
Humiliate the cook in front of everyone
Declare the dish forbidden simply because you dislike it
Demand that all guests share your preference

questions.explanation: Personal taste does not require fault-finding or humiliation.

questions.question: Someone who assists you makes a mistake. Which response reflects the long-term character Anas described?

options.text: Treat their lower position as permission to insult them
Respond with restraint and avoid needless reproach
Make one mistake a reason for constant humiliation
Save respectful treatment only for important visitors

questions.explanation: Anas's memory points toward considerate daily treatment, including relationships with unequal power.

questions.question: A bereaved person is told that crying always shows weak faith. Which Seerah event corrects that claim?

options.text: The sealing of letters to rulers
The appointment of archers at Uhud
The Prophet's tears at Ibrahim's death
The building of Quba Mosque

questions.explanation: The Prophet grieved and shed tears while remaining mindful of speech pleasing to Allah.

questions.question: A learner has not understood an important point. Which teaching approach fits the report from Anas?

options.text: Treat repetition as always beneath a teacher
Increase the speed to finish sooner
Replace explanation with ridicule
Repeat the point clearly to help understanding

questions.explanation: Thoughtful repetition can serve understanding rather than merely repeating for its own sake.

questions.question: You have learned several events from the Prophet's life. What makes the learning more useful?

options.text: Identify a sound lesson and apply it responsibly
Assume recalling names removes every need to act well
Invent dramatic details to make the stories stronger
Treat Seerah only as a competition over dates

questions.explanation: The Quran presents the Messenger as an excellent example; studying his life should inform conduct.

questions.question: Two ways to complete a task are available: one easier but sinful, one lawful. Which qualification in the Prophet's example matters?

options.text: Ease made every choice acceptable
Ease was chosen when it did not involve sin
Difficulty alone was the only measure of goodness
Personal convenience removed every moral limit

questions.explanation: Aishah's report explicitly limits the choice of the easier option to what is not sinful.

questions.question: After harsh rejection, someone urges you to wish ruin on every person involved. Which lesson from the Prophet's response near Taif is relevant?

options.text: Rejection makes all cruelty acceptable
Anger always gives complete knowledge of others' futures
Mercy and hope for future guidance can restrain a desire for revenge
Every rejected request must end all possibility of goodwill

questions.explanation: The Prophet expressed hope that future generations would worship Allah rather than asking for the people's destruction.

questions.question: A loved one feels frightened and overwhelmed. Which response draws on Khadijah's support after revelation?

options.text: Promise that nothing difficult can ever happen again
Dismiss their feelings because respected people cannot be afraid
Make their distress a public spectacle
Listen and offer reassurance grounded in what you know of their goodness

questions.explanation: Khadijah offered caring reassurance and recalled the Prophet's service to others. The lesson is supportive conduct, not a guarantee of a trouble-free life.
